final.memo:
Charlie and I have reviewed the proposed acquisition of the Company, a manufacturer and retailer of footwear [D01]. While we maintain an interest in businesses we can understand, we require a clear view of the underlying economics before committing Berkshire's capital [D01, D05].

In this instance, the fundamental financial records required to assess the business are entirely missing from the pack [D02, D03]. Without audited statements of earnings, cash flow, or a balance sheet, we are unable to calculate owner earnings or verify the existence of a durable competitive advantage [D02, D03].

Furthermore, the footwear industry faces persistent pressure from lower-cost imports, leaving the sustainability of domestic margins an open question [D01]. We have no evidence that the Company possesses the pricing power necessary to maintain a moat against such competition [D01, D05].

Our standard is to buy wonderful businesses at a fair price, not to gamble on speculation [D05]. Because we cannot determine if this $420 million investment offers a margin of safety or will result in the permanent loss of capital, we have decided to pass [D02, D04, D05].
